Class RobotMaze

java.lang.Object
RobotMaze
public class RobotMaze extends Object
A Maze is a SQUARE grid of cells with an entrance, an exit (on the face opposite the entrance), and a set of walls that the player places before starting the game.

Why the maze is square and capped at 7x7:
The Canvas is a fixed 300x300 px window, each cell is CELL_SIZE = 40 px, and the board is drawn starting MARGIN = 10 px from the edge. That means the largest square maze that still fits entirely on screen is (300 - 2*10) / 40 = 7 cells per side (MAX_RECOMMENDED_SIZE). Because of this, the player is only ever asked for one "size" value, which is used as both the number of rows and the number of columns.

Game flow:

  1. The maze is created by specifying a single size (rows = columns). The entrance is placed at random in column 0 (left face) and the exit at random in the opposite column (right face).
  2. The player places walls with addWall(x, y).
  3. The player calls start(): the Robot appears at the entrance with 10 life points, and the board (walls, border, entrance and exit markers) is drawn on the Canvas.
  4. The player repeatedly calls turn(direction) or move().
    • turn(direction) rotates the robot (costs no life).
    • move() attempts to advance one cell in the current direction. If that cell is a wall or outside the maze, the robot does not move and loses 1 life point, and the wall it hit changes color to flag the collision. If it reaches the exit, the player wins. If it runs out of lives, the robot can no longer move and its appearance changes (see Robot.die()).

Reuses the classes from the "shapes" package (Circle, Rectangle, Canvas) only to draw the board. The Robot class itself is reused as built in Part II-A, with the life-management additions (life, getLife(), loseLife(), die()) documented in Robot.java and explained in the lab write-up.

All player-facing input and output goes through JOptionPane dialogs (both the console entry point below and every status/error message raised by the game methods) instead of System.in / System.out.

Bonus — automatic movement and undo:
autoMove() lets the maze decide and execute the robot's next move by itself, delegating to decideBestDirection(), which runs a Breadth-First Search (BFS) over the current wall layout from the robot's cell to the exit. Because every move costs exactly one cell — an unweighted graph — the first path BFS finds to the exit is guaranteed to be the shortest one, so "best move" here simply means "the first step of the shortest known path". undo() reverts the robot to the cell it occupied before its last successful move, using a history stack (moveHistory) filled by saveState(). Undoing counts as a move itself: it is pushed back onto that same stack, so a second undo() call undoes the undo.

  • Constructor Details

    • RobotMaze

      public RobotMaze(int size)
      Creates a SQUARE maze of "size" columns by "size" rows. The entrance is generated at random on the left face (x = 0) and the exit at random on the opposite, right face (x = size - 1). If size is larger than MAX_RECOMMENDED_SIZE, a warning dialog is shown because part of the board will fall outside the 300x300 Canvas.

  • Method Details

    • addWall

      public void addWall(int x, int y)
      Places a wall in cell (x, y). Can only be done before calling start(), and is not allowed on the entrance or exit cell.

    • removeWall

      public void removeWall(int x, int y)
      Removes a previously placed wall at (x, y), if the game has not started.

    • isWall

      public boolean isWall(int x, int y)
      Returns:
      true if cell (x, y) has a wall.

    • start

      public void start()
      Starts the game: places the Robot at the entrance, gives it 10 life points, and draws the whole board (border, walls, entrance and exit markers) on the Canvas.

    • turn

      public void turn(char direction)
      Turns the robot to face a new direction ('N', 'S', 'E', 'W'). Turning costs no life points.

    • move

      public void move()
      Attempts to advance the robot one cell in the direction it is currently facing. If the target cell is a wall or outside the maze, the robot does not move, loses 1 life point, and (if it was a real wall) that wall's color changes to flag the collision. If it reaches the exit, the player wins.

    • quit

      public void quit()
      Ends the current game at the player's request, without the robot having won or run out of lives.

    • isGameOver

      public boolean isGameOver()
      Returns:
      true if the game is over (won, out of lives, or quit).

    • isWon

      public boolean isWon()
      Returns:
      true if the robot reached the exit.

    • getLives

      public int getLives()
      Returns:
      the robot's remaining lives (delegated to Robot.getLife()), or 0 if the game hasn't started.

    • getEntrance

      public int[] getEntrance()
      Returns:
      the {x, y} coordinates of the entrance.

    • getExit

      public int[] getExit()
      Returns:

    • getRobot

      public Robot getRobot()
      Returns:
      the active Robot object (null if the game has not started).

    • main

      public static void main(String[] args)
      Lets the player play RobotMaze entirely through JOptionPane dialogs while the maze and the robot are drawn on the graphical Canvas. It can also be played manually from BlueJ by creating a RobotMaze object in the object bench and calling its methods (addWall, start, turn, move, quit) directly, without using this main.

    • autoMove

      public void autoMove()
      Lets the maze itself decide and execute the robot's next move, using decideBestDirection().

    • undo

      public void undo()
      Undoes the robot's last successful move, returning it to the cell it came from (looked up in moveHistory).

      Per the assignment, undoing counts as a move itself: this method calls saveState() before moving the robot back, so the pre-undo position is pushed onto the same history stack — calling undo() a second time right after undoes the undo.
